focus: Unroll independent or reduction loops and match array partition to the factor.
merge_rule: Union of the 90-skill package and gemm_flatten_v2. On id conflicts, gemm_flatten_v2 replaces the 90-skill entry.

guards: unrolling cannot compensate for insufficient memory bandwidth
check whether the loop is compute-bound before increasing parallelism
avoid unroll factors that exceed memory supply
skills.pattern: the loop is limited by global-memory bandwidth or AXI burst behavior, and adding arithmetic lanes would increase memory pressure without feeding the lanes
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not apply unrolling as the primary optimization; first use coalescing, memory banking, local staging, or tiling to provide enough data bandwidth

guards: do not maximize unroll factor blindly on large arrays
compare latency improvement against resource growth
when backing off from complete unroll on LARGE trip counts, try 32/16/8 before 4/2
on small static PolyBench/ChatHLS mini dims (N<=64), do NOT treat factor=2 as the preferred safe default — prefer complete unroll unless synth util >100%
skills.pattern: a proposed unroll factor replicates too much arithmetic, local storage, or routing and creates excessive DSP/LUT/FF/BRAM usage or timing degradation
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: If complete unroll overflows the device, reduce factor stepwise (32→16→8→4) while keeping partition matched; use factor=2 only as a last resort. For small static dims, complete unroll is usually legal on U280 — do not preemptively cripple parallelism.

guards: applies when inner trip count is a known small constant (typical atax/bicg/mvt/gesummv: 30-42)
still respect true dependences and AXI load bandwidth limits
if complete unroll + matching partition exceeds 100% DSP/FF/LUT/BRAM, then reduce factor
skills.pattern: kernel uses `#pragma HLS UNROLL factor=2` (or similarly tiny factor) on a small compile-time-constant inner loop (e.g. atax/bicg N~38-42) while local arrays are only partially partitioned, leaving most parallelism on the table and high total latency
required_steps: detect tiny partial unroll on small static trip count
replace with `#pragma HLS UNROLL` (complete) on that inner loop
set ARRAY_PARTITION to match (prefer complete on the unrolled dimension)
keep AXI load loops II=1/burst-oriented; do not expect unroll alone to fix gmem
re-synth and confirm util <=100% and lower latency
skills.strategy: Treat UNROLL factor=2 on Mini/ChatHLS-sized static loops as a defect. Use complete unroll + matching partition for on-chip compute; only partial-unroll if util overflows.

guards: unrolling a memory-bound loop can increase pressure without improving latency
fix burst behavior, local reuse, or memory banking before increasing arithmetic parallelism
verify the post-unroll bottleneck is not worse
skills.pattern: II miss or latency is caused by AXI bandwidth, global-memory dependency, or memory-port pressure rather than insufficient arithmetic parallelism
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not respond with large UNROLL or complete partitioning first; route to coalescing, tiling/local staging, memory banking, or local partitioning depending on the true bottleneck

guards: applies to local staging buffers as well as m_axi outputs — same RMW discipline
pair with hls-fp-reduction-partial-accumulators for FP dot-product chains
preserve numerical semantics when splitting partial sums
skills.pattern: matrix-vector or dot-product style loops that update an output accumulator array element inside a pipelined and/or unrolled loop (e.g. local_x[i] += expr under #pragma HLS PIPELINE II=1 or UNROLL over column index j+k)
required_steps: detect local_x[i] += or equivalent in-place update inside PIPELINE II=1 or unrolled j+k loops
allocate partial[UF] per output lane or per unroll lane with #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION complete
accumulate into partial[p] inside the pipelined/unrolled loop
reduce partial[] to a scalar after the loop and write local_x[i] once
do not leave loop-carried dependence on local_x[i] in the hot pipeline
skills.strategy: Never read-modify-write the same local output accumulator element inside a pipelined unrolled loop. Use private partial accumulators with complete partitioning, reduce once after the pipelined loop, then assign local_x[i] exactly once.

skills.pattern: static-bound GEMM/matmul (or 2mm/3mm phase) on locals with PIPELINE on (i,j) (often + LOOP_FLATTEN) and full UNROLL on reduction k, but csynth Final II remains huge (tens–hundreds) because a single float/double accumulator carries a true FP dependence and/or dmul/dadd are resource-shared down to ~1 instance — so latency ≈ trip×II stays catastrophic despite 'k fully unrolled'; also a PIPELINE on k with acc[i][j] += a*b every k (Final II=4) after spatial unroll — csim+csynth pass is not success
skills.strategy: Do not treat full k UNROLL or outer flatten as success when achieved II ≫ 1. Rewrite the reduction with lane/partial sums or a tree (hls-unroll-reduction-partial-sums / ii-reduction-lane-partial-tree), allocate enough FP operators for the chosen parallelism, or fall back to pipeline-on-k with modest outer/j unroll (ChatHLS-style). Re-synth until Final II is near the legal target. Also reject II=4 on a k-pipeline that updates one acc bank every k. Route to k+=4 named acc0..acc3 in one iteration, not switch(k&3), and not more PE_BLK under II=4.
required_steps: detect full k UNROLL under (i,j) pipeline with serial sum += a*b (float/double)
read csynth Final II, accumulator dependence, and dmul/dadd binding/sharing
if Final II ≫ 1 from FP reduction or resource limit, reject the design as optimized
route to partial-sum/tree reduction + matching resources, or pipeline-on-k fallback
re-synth and confirm Final II improved; do not stop at flatten-only success
detect PIPELINE on k with a single acc[i][j] += MAC and Final II=4
reject that as optimized even if DSP is already hundreds
guards: still prefer flatten of sequential outer i when that is the bug (hls-avoid-outer-sequential-gemm-after-inner-pipeline)
preserve numerical tolerance expectations when reassociating FP reductions
device util ≤ 100% after allocating more operators / wider trees
complete partition of a whole large Nd array can destroy timing — prefer partitioning one parallel dim
complete/cyclic on a compile-time k dimension of size ~<=128 for a flattened GEMM is in-scope and often required
do not use resource-heavy partitioning to mask an off-chip bandwidth bottleneck
skills.pattern: a proposed fix completely partitions an entire large local buffer or large multidimensional tile into registers only because there is a memory dependency or port conflict, without targeting the actual parallel access dimension
required_steps: detect whether complete partition is being applied to a large array or large tile
estimate FF/LUT/routing growth from full partitioning
identify the actual parallel access dimension and access count
prefer cyclic/block partitioning, reshape, local banking, or small lane-buffer complete partition
validate whether the alternative resolves II without resource explosion
skills.strategy: do not use complete partition of an entire large buffer as the default; instead partition the parallel access dimension (complete if that dim is modest or required for GEMM flatten; else cyclic/block), or use line buffers / smaller tiles / per-lane small buffers. This avoid-rule does NOT forbid complete/cyclic on GEMM reduction dim k when needed for II=1 flatten.

guards: complete partition on tile buffers larger than the parallel access width is a red flag
triple-nested tile loops with tiny tiles often increase control overhead without improving reuse
this avoid-rule targets micro-tiling with complete partition of tile buffers — not k-dim banking of a full-workspace GEMM
skills.pattern: nested outer tile loops (for example i0, j0, k0) use a small compile-time tile size with ARRAY_PARTITION complete on multidimensional tile buffers and repeated global reloads per tile
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
prefer hls-prefer-full-workspace-staging-when-fits or larger tiles with cyclic or block partition matched to unroll factor
route to ii-avoid-complete-partition-large-buffer-ff-explosion when complete partition inflates resources
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: do not use nested small-tile loops with complete partition as default; prefer hls-prefer-full-workspace-staging-when-fits or larger tiles with cyclic or block partition matched to unroll factor

guards: false-dependence pragmas can silently produce incorrect hardware when applied to true hazards
do not prioritize II=1 over semantic correctness
if exact sequential order is required, algorithmic restructuring may not be legal
skills.pattern: a proposed fix uses DEPENDENCE inter false on an array or accumulator that is truly read and written across iterations, such as a reduction, histogram, in-place update, or same-address read-modify-write
required_steps: check whether two iterations can access the same location with at least one write
classify the dependence as reduction, scatter/RMW, stencil/in-place update, or inherent recurrence
route to partial accumulators, privatization, old/new buffering, wavefront, or best-legal-II handling
remove unsafe false-dependence pragma proposals
validate correctness before measuring II
skills.strategy: reject the false-dependence pragma and use a legal transformation instead: partial sums for reductions, privatized accumulators for RMW/scatter, old/new buffers for Jacobi-style updates, or accept the legal II for inherently serial recurrences

guards: choose UF to match available DSP/budget
preserve numerics within acceptable reordering for independent partials
skills.pattern: floating-point reduction or accumulation into one scalar inside a loop claimed II=1 (e.g. w -= a*b, sum += expr, acc = acc + expr as the only accumulation chain)
required_steps: detect FP update statements that read and write the same scalar accumulator in the pipelined loop
allocate partial[UF] with complete partition
unroll init and per-lane updates inside pipelined fixed-bound loops
reduce partial[] after the pipelined loop
skills.strategy: Do not accumulate into a single scalar inside a pipelined loop. Use private partial accumulators with complete ARRAY_PARTITION, unrolled init/update, then a final tree or serial reduction.

skills.pattern: PIPELINE II=1 on a k-loop that does acc[i][j] += a*b (or C[i][j] +=) every k. Csynth Final II=4 from the float MAC recurrence. Spatial unroll (16x32) may already be present; DSP may already be hundreds. csim and csynth still pass
skills.strategy: Reject the kernel as optimized. II=4 on the reduction is not a legal endpoint. Route to hls-fp-mac-k-step-independent-acc-banks. More DSPs or a wider tile under II=4 does not close II.
required_steps: detect red_k / compute_k PIPELINE with acc[i][j] += every k
read csynth: pipelined yes, Final II=4, HLS 200-880 carried dependence
do not accept csim+csynth success as done
rewrite with k += 4 and named acc0..acc3 updated in one iteration
guards: DEPENDENCE inter false is not the fix
DSP fill / PE_BLK widening under II=4 is not the fix
inherently serial integer recurrences are out of scope

skills.pattern: the rewrite splits acc0..acc3 but still uses for (k=0; k<K; ++k) PIPELINE with switch(k&3) / acc[k%4], so only one bank is written per iteration. HLS reports carried dependence distance=1 and Final II=4
skills.strategy: Reject switch(k&3) as the II=4 fix. Distance-4 is not visible to the scheduler in that form (observed: II=4 on acc2). Emit k += 4 and update all four named banks in the same pipeline iteration.
required_steps: detect switch(k & 3) or acc[k%4] under a k++ PIPELINE
do not treat four named arrays as success unless k advances by 4 in the body
route to hls-fp-mac-k-step-independent-acc-banks
guards: named acc0..acc3 are necessary but not sufficient
do not add DEPENDENCE inter false to paper over the switch
preserve numerical semantics when staging into locals
const read-only m_axi inputs may be read once per tile into locals
in-place outputs still require local write-back buffers, not inner-loop RMW on the port
skills.pattern: compute loops perform read-modify-write updates directly on arrays mapped to m_axi ports (e.g. A[i][j] = A[i][j] + expr, x[i] = x[i] + expr, w[i] = w[i] + expr inside nested loops)
required_steps: scan every loop for statements that read and write the same m_axi port element
reject direct accumulation into m_axi arrays
reject repeated reads of the same output element from DRAM/HBM inside an inner loop
reject repeated writes to the same output element inside an inner loop
replace with load-compute-store using local buffers or private scalar accumulators
for reductions, accumulate in a private scalar or local array, then write back once
if the full array is too large, tile/block but still finalize each tile locally before one store
skills.strategy: Treat every m_axi argument as external DRAM/HBM. Never read and write the same external element inside an inner loop. Do not use global/m_axi arrays as temporary storage or assume HLS will cache m_axi data across iterations.

guards: do not include source benchmark names in agent-visible prompts
do not encode baseline-to-target sequences in skill IDs
do not expose private evaluator metadata
skills.pattern: agent attempts to infer or mention the source benchmark suite, hidden test design, target variant sequence, or expected optimization step from skill names or evaluation feedback
required_steps: detect whether this avoid-rule pattern is present
do not apply the unsafe or superficial transformation
route to a safer skill based on the actual bottleneck
validate with synthesis and correctness feedback
skills.strategy: optimize only from current code, reports, constraints, and feedback; do not assume a benchmark family, stepwise target, or one-shot target

guards: avoid-tier skills must not cause fallback to unoptimized reference code
when in doubt, apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate rather than emitting textbook C
skills.pattern: the model avoids advanced transforms because of many avoid rules or uncertainty, and responds with textbook nested loops on global arrays and no compute pragmas
required_steps: detect reference-port output despite loaded skill catalog
do not treat caution as permission to skip optimization
apply hls-baseline-load-compute-store-gate, hls-multi-phase-local-pipeline, or hls-iterative-stencil-timestep-local-volume as appropriate
ensure PIPELINE pragmas exist before submitting
skills.strategy: avoid rules forbid unsafe transforms, not all transforms; when uncertain, still apply the baseline local load-compute-store recipe instead of reference C
